MbcoMIResult: D4-stacked MBCO test result (S7)

Source: R/MbcoMIResult.R
MbcoMIResult.Rd

The value of infer(<MDMediationFit>, type = "mbco") and mbco_d4(), for the glm and the lavaan (maximum likelihood) engines alike. It is an S7 object whose parent is class_double: its data is the named numeric vector c(D4, p, r4, nu, d_S), and the properties carry how it was computed and the branch diagnostics.

Usage

MbcoMIResult(
  .data = numeric(0),
  ariv = character(0),
  k = integer(0),
  m = integer(0),
  stacked_branch = character(0),
  branch_mix = logical(0),
  p_branch_a = integer(0)
)

Arguments

.data

Named numeric c(D4, p, r4, nu, d_S).

ariv

"fixed" or "own": which per-imputation statistics fed r4 (see mbco_d4()).

k

Number of parameters the constraint removes (numerator df).

m

Number of imputations pooled.

stacked_branch

"a" or "b": the branch (a = 0 or b = 0) chosen by the constrained fit on the stacked data.

branch_mix

Logical; TRUE when the imputations disagree on their own winning branch.

p_branch_a

Share of imputations whose own winning branch is a = 0.

Value

An MbcoMIResult S7 object.

Details

  • D4: the pooled statistic, referred to \(F(k, \nu)\).

  • p: its p-value.

  • r4: the relative increase in variance, clamped at 0.

  • nu: the denominator degrees of freedom (Inf when r4 is 0).

  • d_S: the MBCO statistic on the stacked data divided by the number of imputations.

x["p"], x[["p"]] and is.numeric(x) work as they did on the plain vector returned by missingmed 0.4.0 and earlier, and S7::S7_data(x) returns that vector. Two things differ: identical(x, old_vector) is FALSE, and x$p is an error.

See also

infer(), mbco_d4()

Examples

r <- MbcoMIResult(c(D4 = 4.7, p = 0.048, r4 = 1.16, nu = 13.8, d_S = 10.2),
  ariv = "fixed", k = 1, m = 5, stacked_branch = "b",
  branch_mix = TRUE, p_branch_a = 0.4
)
r[["p"]]
#> [1] 0.048
r@stacked_branch
#> [1] "b"
